title: Conformance corpus under --engine auto --confirm: JBMC's word on every proof of the own checker, held to the JVM
description: Step 1e of llm-dlc/loops/sound-verdicts.md adds --confirm to --engine auto: JBMC proves again, in one run over every input, each statement the tool's own checker proved, and a JBMC refutation is reported as neither verdict (unverifiable, 'the engines disagree'). This job runs the ignored test the_corpus_agrees_with_the_jvm_under_auto_confirm over the 93 claims of the conformance corpus (lib/tests/conformance.rs), under --gaps strict and --gaps assume. Every witness and claim is also run on a real JVM. The test fails on a JBMC confirmation of a claim the JVM refutes, and on a disagreement over a claim the JVM does not refute. Under assume, the class-initializer claims boom and inherited should come out as disagreements (JBMC runs the initializer the own checker assumed had run), and the claims that assumed a JDK call should be not-asked.
expected: exits 0: the_corpus_agrees_with_the_jvm_under_auto_confirm passes. The log's table shows a confirmation status per claim; under assume, boom and inherited are Disagreed and the JDK-call claims NotAsked. A failure lists each disagreement with the JVM, a finding about JBMC or the adapter to triage under the brief's Progress, not something to retry.

resources.notes: about 90 single-stage JBMC runs on methods of a line or two (each claim the own checker proves, under two gap modes), plus the native runs, which take 11 s for the corpus in the session

steps.name: conformance corpus under auto --confirm
steps.run: set -o pipefail; cd lib && JVMCONTRACT_JBMC_MEMORY_MB=2048 cargo test --release --test conformance the_corpus_agrees_with_the_jvm_under_auto_confirm -- --ignored --nocapture 2>&1 | tee target/conformance-confirm.log
